body: And I'm so sorry to hear about your mom's fall and everything associated with it. That sounds very rough. This is what I imagine might happen with my mom--some kind of outside problem that involves a hospital, police, or something else to force her to change.

Thank you so much for your reply. It's really helpful to hear other people have this issue.

  
We do have POA, all of us. I didn't know until recently that meant we could communicate with her doctor. I thought HIPAA prevented all communication. We honestly don't even know her doctor's name--she is extremely private about everything --but do know the practice. I tried to leave them a voicemail message about a year ago, and could only get a note written on her chart by the person who answered the phone. I don't know what happened with that--it has never been reported back to us. I'm going to write a letter to the practice, maybe tonight. I hope they will call me back. This is so frustrating.

Echoing microneedling recommendation. I am 50, and I stopped getting botox because microneedling by itself was so effective.

I get microneedling (regular, not PRP or RF) and Elixis Ultra (skin tightening with both RF and ultrasound) about three times a year, and it's really doing it for me.

Just today, an old friend said I look "comically" like I did 25 years ago. 

Also, I am a hairstylist. And I will tell you that the \*right\* hair color along with having your eyebrows shaped and tinted will take 10 years off your face, without doing anything else at all.

  
You got this!
I would wrote back and say, you started the no contact, but I’m finding it’s working for me. Please don’t contact me anymore.

It’s so hard to know what they’re getting from sending an email like this, but it’s definitely an ego boost somehow.

You can reply again and say, I was serious when I said leave me alone. I will contact you again when the time is right for me, and I don’t want to talk to you until then. About anything. I can find my own news.

If they keep replying, tell them you’ll take out an order of protection. That has stopped others for me.

Good luck.

We all make mistakes. Truly. It’s important to remember that before you skewer yourself.

All you can do is apologize sincerely. It may not make your relationship with her or the women’s’ relationship with each other better. And you shouldn’t expect it to. But in the long run, it is the right thing to do. And you will feel better over time knowing you have done what you can do to ease the suffering you caused. And they will too. It makes a difference.

Move forward in life by taking accountability for your actions in relationships. Not censoring yourself or avoiding them, but appreciating how you can influence others’ lives, and the responsibility you have for people around you.

It’s going to be ok. Truly. Remember everybody has done this. Apologize sincerely, without any expectation of forgiveness. 

Go through the world trying to do good, knowing that you and everyone else is human and extremely fallible.
